subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class browser-plugin config for per-profile proxy settings plus per-agent/subagent browser-profile binding, or should this remain external orchestration through remote CDP, multiple gateways, node profiles, or ClawHub-style packages?
rationale: Current source proves the requested capability is still missing, but the implementation would define public config, proxy secret handling, browser egress trust, and agent/session ownership semantics that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Design Core Browser Contract
options.body: Approve a first-class browser-plugin design for proxy secrets, per-agent inheritance, concurrency limits, tab ownership, and diagnostics before implementation.

options.title: Split Canonical Work
options.body: Keep this as an umbrella and move proxy transport/security to the broader proxy issue while subagent ownership stays in the dedicated subagent browser issue.

options.title: Defer To External Orchestration
options.body: Document remote CDP, multiple gateways, browser-lock-style wrappers, or ClawHub packages as the supported path and close only after maintainers decide not to add core config.

recommendation.title: Design Core Browser Contract
recommendation.body: Approve a first-class browser-plugin design for proxy secrets, per-agent inheritance, concurrency limits, tab ownership, and diagnostics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across browser profile config, browser plugin ownership, docs, and the security-sensitive control path.
